source.title: Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible
source.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset and David Brown
source.edition: CCEL expanded electronic edition of the 1871 public-domain text

entries.heading: 2. darkness
entries.text: 2. darkness --calamity. light --prosperity.

entries.heading: 3. turneth . . . hand
entries.text: 3. turneth . . . hand --to inflict again and again new strokes. "His hand," which once used to protect me. "Turned . . . turneth" implies repeated inflictions.

entries.heading: Verse 4
entries.text: Beth.

entries.heading: 5. builded
entries.text: 5. builded --mounds, as against a besieged city, so as to allow none to escape (so La 3:7, 9 ).

entries.heading: 6. set me
entries.text: 6. set me --Henderson refers this to the custom of placing the dead in a sitting posture. dark places --sepulchers. As those "dead long since"; so Jeremiah and his people are consigned to oblivion ( Ps 88:5, 6; 143:3; Eze 37:13 ).

entries.heading: Verse 7
entries.text: Gimel.

entries.heading: 8. shutteth out
entries.text: 8. shutteth out --image from a door shutting out any entrance ( Job 30:20 ). So the antitype. Christ ( Ps 22:2 ).

entries.heading: 9. hewn stone
entries.text: 9. hewn stone --which coheres so closely as not to admit of being broken through. paths crooked --thwarted our plans and efforts so that none went right.

entries.heading: Verse 10
entries.text: Daleth.

entries.heading: 11. turned aside
entries.text: 11. turned aside --made me wander out of the right way, so as to become a prey to wild beasts. pulled in pieces -- ( Ho 6:1 ), as a "bear" or a "lion" ( La 3:10 ).

entries.heading: Verse 13
entries.text: He.
14. ( Jer 20:7 ). their song -- ( Ps 69:12 ). Jeremiah herein was a type of Messiah. "All my people" ( Joh 1:11 ).

entries.heading: 15. wormwood
entries.text: 15. wormwood -- ( Jer 9:15 ). There it is regarded as food, namely, the leaves: here as drink, namely, the juice.

entries.heading: Verse 16
entries.text: Vau.
17. Not only present, but all hope of future prosperity is removed; so much so, that I am as one who never was prosperous ("I forgat prosperity").

entries.heading: 18. from the Lord
entries.text: 18. from the Lord --that is, my hope derived from Him ( Ps 31:22 ).

entries.heading: Verse 19
entries.text: Zain.
20. As often as my soul calls them to remembrance, it is humbled or bowed down in me.

entries.heading: 21. This
entries.text: 21. This --namely, what follows; the view of the divine character ( La 3:22, 23 ). Calvin makes "this" refer to Jeremiah's infirmity. His very weakness ( La 3:19, 20 ) gives him hope of God interposing His strength for him (compare Ps 25:11, 17; 42:5, 8; 2Co 12:9, 10 ).

entries.heading: Verse 22
entries.text: Cheth.
24. ( Nu 18:20; Ps 16:5; 73:26; 119:57; Jer 10:16 ). To have God for our portion is the one only foundation of hope.

entries.heading: Verse 25
entries.text: Teth.

entries.heading: 26. quietly wait
entries.text: 26. quietly wait --literally, "be in silence." Compare La 3:28 and Ps 39:2, 9 , that is, to be patiently quiet under afflictions, resting in the will of God ( Ps 37:7 ). So Aaron ( Le 10:2, 3 ); and Job ( Job 40:4, 5 ).

entries.heading: 27. yoke
entries.text: 27. yoke --of the Lord's disciplinary teaching ( Ps 90:12; 119:71 ). Calvin interprets it, The Lord's doctrine ( Mt 11:29, 30 ), which is to be received in a docile spirit. The earlier the better; for the old are full of prejudices ( Pr 8:17; Ec 12:1 ). Jeremiah himself received the yoke, both of doctrine and chastisement in his youth ( Jer 1:6, 7 ).

entries.heading: Verse 28
entries.text: Jod.

29. ( Job 42:6 ). The mouth in the dust is the attitude of suppliant and humble submission to God's dealings as righteous and loving in design (compare Ezr 9:6; 1Co 14:25 ). if so be there may be hope --This does not express doubt as to whether God be willing to receive the penitent, but the penitent's doubt as to himself; he whispers to himself this consolation, "Perhaps there may be hope for me."

30. Messiah, the Antitype, fulfilled this; His practice agreeing with His precept ( Isa 50:6; Mt 5:39 ). Many take patiently afflictions from God, but when man wrongs them, they take it impatiently. The godly bear resignedly the latter, like the former, as sent by God ( Ps 17:13 ).

entries.heading: Verse 31
entries.text: Caph.
32. The punishments of the godly are but for a time.
33. He does not afflict any willingly (literally, "from His heart," that is, as if He had any pleasure in it, Eze 33:11 ), much less the godly ( Heb 12:10 ).

entries.heading: Verse 34
entries.text: Lamed.

entries.heading: 35. before . . . face of . . . most High
entries.text: 35. before . . . face of . . . most High --Any "turning aside" of justice in court is done before the face of God, who is present, and "regardeth," though unseen ( Ec 5:8 ).

entries.heading: 36. subvert
entries.text: 36. subvert --to wrong.

entries.heading: Verse 37
entries.text: Mem.

entries.heading: 38. evil . . . good
entries.text: 38. evil . . . good -- Calamity and prosperity alike proceed from God ( Job 2:10; Isa 45:7; Am 3:6 ).

entries.heading: 39. living
entries.text: 39. living --and so having a time yet given him by God for repentance. If sin were punished as it deserves, life itself would be forfeited by the sinner. "Complaining" (murmuring) ill becomes him who enjoys such a favor as life ( Pr 19:3 ). for the punishment of his sins --Instead of blaming God for his sufferings, he ought to recognize in them God's righteousness and the just rewards of his own sin.

entries.heading: Verse 40
entries.text: Nun.

entries.heading: 41. heart with . . . hands
entries.text: 41. heart with . . . hands --the antidote to hypocrisy ( Ps 86:4; 1Ti 2:8 ).

entries.heading: 42. not pardoned
entries.text: 42. not pardoned --The Babylonian captivity had not yet ended.

entries.heading: Verse 43
entries.text: Samech.
44. ( La 3:8 ). The "cloud" is our sins, and God's wrath because of them ( Isa 44:22; 59:2 ).
45. So the apostles were treated; but, instead of murmuring, they rejoiced at it ( 1Co 4:13 ).

entries.heading: Verse 46
entries.text: Pe.
47. Like animals fleeing in fear, we fall into the snare laid for us.

entries.heading: Verse 49
entries.text: Ain.

entries.heading: 50. Till
entries.text: 50. Till --His prayer is not without hope, wherein it differs from the blind grief of unbelievers. look down, &c.-- ( Isa 63:15 ).

entries.heading: 51. eye affecteth mine heart
entries.text: 51. eye affecteth mine heart --that is, causeth me grief with continual tears; or, "affecteth my life " (literally, "soul," Margin ), that is, my health [Grotius]. daughters of . . . city --the towns around, dependencies of Jerusalem, taken by the foe.

entries.heading: Verse 52
entries.text: Tzaddi.

entries.heading: 53. in . . . dungeon
entries.text: 53. in . . . dungeon -- ( Jer 37:16 ). stone --usually put at the mouth of a dungeon to secure the prisoners ( Jos 10:18; Da 6:17; Mt 27:60 ).

entries.heading: 54. Waters
entries.text: 54. Waters --not literally, for there was "no water" ( Jer 38:6 ) in the place of Jeremiah's confinement, but emblematical of overwhelming calamities ( Ps 69:2; 124:4, 5 ). cut off -- ( Isa 38:10, 11 ). I am abandoned by God. He speaks according to carnal sense.

entries.heading: Verse 55
entries.text: Koph.

entries.heading: 56. Thou hast heard
entries.text: 56. Thou hast heard --namely formerly (so in La 3:57, 58 ). breathing . . . cry --two kinds of prayer; the sigh of a prayer silently breathed forth, and the loud, earnest cry (compare "prayer," " secret speech, " Isa 26:16 , Margin; with "cry aloud," Ps 55:17 ).

entries.heading: 57. Thou drewest near
entries.text: 57. Thou drewest near --with Thy help ( Jas 4:8 ).

entries.heading: Verse 58
entries.text: Resh.
59. God's past deliverances and His knowledge of Judah's wrongs are made the grounds of prayer for relief.

entries.heading: 60. imaginations
entries.text: 60. imaginations --devices ( Jer 11:19 ). Their vengeance --means their malice. Jeremiah gives his conduct, when plotted against by his foes, as an example how the Jews should bring their wrongs at the hands of the Chaldeans before God.

entries.heading: Verse 61
entries.text: Schin.

entries.heading: 62. lips
entries.text: 62. lips --speeches.

entries.heading: 63. sitting down . . . rising up
entries.text: 63. sitting down . . . rising up --whether they sit or rise, that is, whether they be actively engaged or sedentary, and at rest "all the day" ( La 3:62 ), I am the subject of their derisive songs ( La 3:14 ).

entries.heading: Verse 64
entries.text: Tau.

entries.heading: 65. sorrow
entries.text: 65. sorrow --rather, blindness or hardness; literally, "a veil" covering their heart, so that they may rush on to their own ruin ( Isa 6:10; 2Co 3:14, 15 ).

entries.heading: 66. from under . . . heavens of . . . Lord
entries.text: 66. from under . . . heavens of . . . Lord -- destroy them so that it may be seen everywhere under heaven that thou sittest above as Judge of the world.
